candidates.title: Design and mechanical analysis of the PRAGYA tokamak vacuum vessel
candidates.notes: Accessible peer-reviewed preprint (March 12, 2026) by Shaurya Kaushal et al. Provides first published machine parameters for PRAGYA: R0≈0.4 m, a>0.18 m, Ip up to 25 kA, B_T=0.1 T. Structural FEM analysis of vacuum vessel under atmospheric pressure, thermal, and self-weight loads. Does not describe JENGA directly, but is the first substantive published technical document from Pranos. Establishes machine geometry for the experimental PRAGYA device (not the commercial 50 MW vision).

candidates.title: Why we invested in Pranos Fusion — Ankur Capital
candidates.notes: Investor rationale post. Confirms '20+ Tesla HTS magnets' (resolving gap 3 — magnet type — as HTS confirmed). Describes JENGA as microsecond-level plasma control software. No machine parameters or JENGA output data. Qualitative only. Not extracted — no quantitative data warranting extraction as a standalone source.

candidates.title: Pranos Nets $6.8 Mn To Build Tokamak, Superconducting Magnets For Nuclear Fusion — inc42
candidates.notes: News article on Series A round ($6.8M from pi Ventures, Ankur Capital, Industrial47, Groww co-founder, Razorpay founders, Bhukhanwala Industries). Analysis currently records only $417K seed — this is a major update. PRAGYA described as 'not suitable for actual fusion' (experimental testing device only). JENGA described as likely first revenue product. Not extracted — no quantitative technical data beyond funding figures.

extracted.notes: Extracted to iter-02/sources/arxiv-2603-11549.md. Peer-reviewed preprint; first published technical document from Pranos Fusion. Provides PRAGYA machine geometry (R0≈0.4 m, a>0.18 m) — critical for analysis sections S1/S2/S5 even though PRAGYA is an experimental device, not the 50 MW commercial concept.

gaps_attempted.analyst_notes: Gap 14 specifically targets Jenga digital twin validation outputs. No JENGA-specific preprint or model output was found. The arXiv paper addresses vacuum vessel structural design (FEM), not JENGA simulation outputs. However, it is the only published technical document from Pranos Fusion and provides machine parameters for PRAGYA (R0=0.4 m) which incidentally helps anchor several other blocking gaps (G-1 machine geometry, G-3 magnet type via Ankur Capital confirmation). Gap 14 remains open in the strict sense — no JENGA model outputs have been published as of April 2026.

incidental_findings.finding: Funding update: Pranos Fusion has raised $6.8M Series A (pi Ventures + Ankur Capital co-lead, April 2026), up from the $417K seed recorded in the current analysis. This is a ~16× funding increase and materially changes the company's financial position and credibility assessment.

HTS magnet type confirmed: Ankur Capital investor post states '20+ Tesla HTS magnets' — resolving Gap 3 (magnet type) from 'proprietary/unknown' to 'HTS confirmed' for MAGGA program. Aligns with ST-HTS analogue assumption already applied in analysis.

PRAGYA experimental machine parameters published (arXiv 2603.11549): R0≈0.4 m, a>0.18 m, Ip≤25 kA, B_T=0.1 T. Aspect ratio A = R0/a < 2.2 — confirms low aspect ratio (spherical tokamak) classification. Note: PRAGYA is an experimental device explicitly described as 'not suitable for actual fusion' (inc42); it is not the commercial 50 MW PRANIQ concept. These parameters cannot be directly applied to LCOE modeling but confirm the ST geometry and provide a development baseline.

First plasma on PRAGYA targeted for 2026 (multiple sources). Company is manufacturing vacuum vessel through Ranvac (fusion vessel experience confirmed by Ankur Capital). Development stage is more advanced than 'glass globe plasma' characterization in current analysis — vacuum vessel FEM complete, manufacturing contracted.

summary.notes: Only one not-yet-sourced gap (G-14) existed in the Section 6 inventory. No JENGA validation outputs were found publicly — Gap 14 remains partially open. The arXiv preprint (2603.11549) is the highest-value find: first peer-reviewed technical document from Pranos with machine geometry. Several incidental findings of significance were identified: $6.8M funding round (vs $417K in current analysis), HTS magnet type confirmation, and PRAGYA experimental parameters.
